notes:
disagreement: value: the parent cell of the three topic details: one pass finds the parent by the name Global Assignments, the other by id 13; chose 13, the tighter, which names the row the category requirement anchors; the category requirement therefore also carries the topic details check, whose join on the category's name it tests (resolved on those requirements).
disagreement: value: the HR service's template cell: one pass finds the template by name, the other by id 7; chose 7, the tighter, which names the row the template requirement anchors; the template requirement therefore also carries the HR service check, whose join on the template's name it tests (resolved on those requirements).
disagreement: disposition: the approval criterion check: one pass repaired it (group pinned to HR Service Desk), the other kept it while testing the same group 4; chose repaired, since the query as written accepts Global Service Desk and HR Case Readers, which the request does not name.
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id and cell; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The visibility criterion is to cover both the HR Service Desk group and the Infrastructure Problem Team groups (Network Infrastructure, group 7, and Server Operations, group 8, in organization 1), but hr_criteria holds one user_group; the second part can only go into the users JSON column (members of groups 7 and 8 are users 29, 33, 38 and 40), whose storage format the seed does not show (every seed criterion has users empty), so that cell is untestable and left out.
The policy's enumeration for hr_service.fulfillment_type lists workflow, approval, manual and integration only, and every seed service is manual; the request and the benchmark both ask for lifecycle event, so the requirement keeps that value. The same enumeration section also disagrees with values the seed stores (user roles admin and manager, case priorities moderate and planning), so it is not treated as binding; a server that enforced it would reject the value.
The requested names (Global Assignments and the topic detail names) are shorter than the policy's 30-character minimum for titles; the request gives them verbatim and they are tested as given.
